name: fwrule_analyze
description: Analyze a firewall/ACL rule set OFFLINE for shadowing, redundancy, duplicate, and conflicting rules. In the code sandbox this is exposed as the pre-bound `fwrule` object: fwrule.analyze(acl_text, vendor='ios') to parse Cisco IOS/IOS-XE ACLs, or fwrule.analyze(rules=[{action,protocol,src,dst,src_port,dst_port}, ...]) for a normalized rule list from any vendor. Returns {ok, rule_count, findings:[{type, earlier, later, detail}], summary:{shadowing, redundancy, duplicate, conflict}}. No network, no credentials.

function.name: fwrule_analyze
function.description: Offline firewall/ACL rule analyzer. Exposed as the `fwrule` object in the sandbox — call fwrule.analyze(...). Detects, via 6-dimension set intersection (protocol, src net, src port, dst net, dst port, action): shadowing (earlier rule fully covers a later rule with the OPPOSITE action -> later can never match), redundancy (earlier covers later, SAME action -> later is unnecessary), duplicate (identical match + action), conflict (overlapping rules with opposite actions -> order-dependent). Input EITHER acl_text (Cisco IOS/IOS-XE extended ACL CLI, vendor='ios') OR rules=[{action, protocol, src, dst, src_port, dst_port}] (normalized, any vendor; src/dst are CIDR or 'any', ports are int/[lo,hi]/'any'). Returns {ok, rule_count, findings, summary}.

acl_text.description: Raw ACL CLI text to parse (use with vendor). Cisco IOS/IOS-XE extended ACLs supported.

vendor.description: Vendor for acl_text parsing (default 'ios'). Only IOS/IOS-XE CLI parsing is implemented; for others pass rules=.

rules.description: Normalized rule list [{action, protocol, src, dst, src_port, dst_port}] for any vendor.
